## 1. Load and inspect the data

Load the built-in dataset.

```{r}
# Load the built-in mtcars dataset into the session
data(mtcars)
```

Look at the first rows.

```{r}
# Show the first 6 rows so we can see the columns and their values
head(mtcars)
```

Check the structure of the data.

```{r}
# Show each variable's type and a preview of its values
str(mtcars)
```

Summarize the variables we will use.

```{r}
# Print min, quartiles, median, mean, and max for mpg, wt, and hp
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

## 2. Explore relationships

Scatterplot matrix.

```{r}
# Plot every pair of variables to check for roughly linear relationships
pairs(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

Correlation matrix.

```{r}
# Compute pairwise correlations (values near -1 or 1 mean strong linear relationships)
cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

## 3. Fit the model

Fit the multiple linear regression.

```{r}
# Fit a linear model: predict mpg from wt (weight) and hp (horsepower)
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
```

View the results.

```{r}
# Show coefficients, p-values, R-squared, and the overall F-test
summary(model)
```

Confidence intervals.

```{r}
# Show 95% confidence intervals for the intercept and each slope
confint(model)
```

## 4. Check assumptions

Diagnostic plots.


```{r}
# Set the plotting area to a 2x2 grid so all four plots show together
par(mfrow = c(4, 4))

# Draw the four standard diagnostic plots for the model
# (residuals vs fitted, Q-Q, scale-location, residuals vs leverage)
plot(model)

```

Load the package for multicollinearity.

```{r}
# Load the car package (run install.packages("car") once if it is missing)
install.packages("car")
library(car)
```

Multicollinearity check.

```{r}
# Compute variance inflation factors (values above about 5 suggest a problem)
vif(model)
```

Normality of residuals.

```{r}
# Test whether residuals are normal (p > 0.05 means no evidence against normality)
shapiro.test(residuals(model))
```

## 5. Interpretation

- **Intercept:** The predicted mpg for a car with weight 0 and horsepower 0. It is not realistic, just a baseline for the line.
- **wt:** Holding horsepower constant, each additional 1000 lbs is associated with about a 3.9 mpg decrease.
- **hp:** Holding weight constant, each additional horsepower is associated with about a 0.03 mpg decrease.
- **R²:** Weight and horsepower together explain about 83% of the variation in mpg.
- **Assumptions:** (describe what you see in the diagnostic plots, VIF, and Shapiro test)
- **Caveat:** These are associations, not causation, and the data is only 32 cars from 1974.
